summary.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q2 FY27 adjusted consolidated PAT rose to ₹333 crore, with India PAT up 62% (adjusted ₹330 crore vs ₹262 crore reported last year).
summary.overview: Management described Q2 as strong, with same-store sales growth above 20% and a shifted festive season. Consolidated revenue was ₹10,323 crore (adjusted ₹9,943 crore), and adjusted consolidated EBITDA was ₹593 crore against ₹497 crore a year earlier per the call's figures. India revenue rose to ₹9,007 crore from ₹6,843 crore, and the Middle East business posted revenue of ₹960 crore versus ₹860 crore. Management said Dhanteras, Navratri and the post-Navratri weekend were strong and early Q3 momentum remains good, while reiterating a 25% revenue growth target for the year without giving a numeric guidance for Q3 or Q4.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹9,007 crore vs ₹6,843 crore YoY; reported PAT ₹424 crore, up 62%, with adjusted PAT ₹330 crore. Same-store sales growth was above 20% in Q2.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹960 crore (vs ₹860 crore) and EBITDA ₹71 crore (vs ₹61 crore), but profit fell to ₹12 crore from ₹15 crore.

segments.name: ATM (regional brand, Tamil Nadu)
segments.commentary: Launched at Chinnanagar, Chennai in August; management says performance has exceeded expectations, but no metrics were disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth target of about 25%, reiterated as a target rather than numeric guidance; management said H1 was ahead of expectations.
Same-store sales growth of about 10% for Q4 is still the planning assumption; Q3 is tracking better than estimates.
PBT margins expected to be stable in H2, and higher than H1 as is seasonally typical.
Gold-on-cash (GOC) share of exchange rose to 42%, with gold-on-cash at 7-8% of exchange, supporting margin stability.
Store additions: two ATM showrooms in Q3 and two in Q4 FY27; store inaugurations are weighted toward H2, especially Q4.
Non-GML (non-gold-metal-loan) debt is fully repaid; 50% of the collateral land is released, with one parcel sold for ~₹86-87 crore and ₹16 crore more expected in Q3.
capex_capacity: Four new ATM showrooms planned in FY27: two in Q3 and two in Q4; ATM is limited to Tamil Nadu for now, with no immediate plans for another state.
Surplus cash to go toward strengthening existing showrooms, with more inventory in certain stores and a few flagship stores, after none in the last two to three years.
Cash-flow deployment plan to be shared shortly for FY28.
Remaining land parcel (50% of collateral) to be released soon, with the process already started.
demand_pricing: Dhanteras, Navratri and the post-Navratri weekend were strong; management declined to give a Q3 growth number but said growth on the ground is excellent.
Management said the first 40 days of the festive period showed volume growth, with consumers buying more volume within the same budget as gold prices eased.
Gold price inflation was in single digits in Q2 (versus SSG above 20%), so growth has been volume-led.
Wedding-related purchases are about 60% of the mix; wedding buyers defer for 15-20 days during price volatility, then buy.
Management says it is gaining market share post-COVID and benefiting from a shift from unorganized to organized; about 60% of the market remains unorganized.
Coin sales are a single-digit share of revenue; the Tamil Nadu one-gram gold coin contract for childbirth has begun generating small B2B revenue at thin margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is festive growth tracking ahead of the strong SSG, and how should Q3 and Q4 trajectory be considered against the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Dhanteras, Navratri and post-Navratri were very good and growth is continuing, and it is very confident of meeting its targeted revenue growth. It repeated the ~10% SSG planning assumption and a 25% annual revenue growth target, not a number for Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is PBT margin recovery sustainable given exchange gains and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Adjusted for customs duty gains and silver/platinum gains in the prior year, Q2 margins were stable. Gold-on-cash rose to 42% of exchange, and management expects H2 PBT margins to be better than H1 and stable.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gold price moderation affecting buying behaviour and LFL throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers come with a fixed budget and buy more volume when gold is cheaper; Q2 SSG was above 20% with single-digit gold inflation, and volume growth continued into the first 40 days of the festive period.

qa_highlights.question: Can ATM performance metrics and roll-out plans be shared, and what is the cash deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: ATM performance has exceeded expectations, but management did not share metrics given competitive sensitivity; four more showrooms are planned in FY27. No plans for another state; cash to go to existing showrooms and flagships, with a plan for FY28 to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong demand from market share gains, and how is the mix changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed market share gains since COVID, a shift from unorganized to organized, and a move toward studded and design-led jewellery, with coins a single-digit share of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tamil Nadu gold coin contract's revenue timing and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue has started but is very small; the business is B2B with thin margins, and the aim is brand visibility rather than margin.

risks_watch: Q4 faces a high base; growth depends on wedding-season momentum and H2 store openings concentrated in Q4.
Gold price volatility can cause wedding buyers to defer purchases, which affects timing of demand.
Middle East profit declined to ₹12 crore from ₹15 crore despite revenue and EBITDA growth.
Competitive intensity in making charges and discounts remains high; management says it responds case by case.
Quality of PAT growth: reported PAT includes one-off customs duty and exceptional items, so adjusted figures should be tracked.
Monitor the sale of the remaining land parcel and the FY28 cash-flow allocation plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on festive and Q3 momentum, but deliberately non-numeric on Q3/Q4 growth and ATM metrics, citing competitive sensitivity.
key_quotes: We are very confident of meeting the targeted revenue growth.
Q1 was better than estimate, Q2 was better than estimate, Q3 as we speak is better than estimates.
So we believe that H2 will be of a better PBT margin than H1.
No more immediate plans to go to another state.

adds.what: Four new ATM showrooms (regional brand, Tamil Nadu): two in Q3 FY27, two in Q4 FY27

growth.why: Management reiterated a ~25% full-year revenue growth target (a target, not numeric guidance) with H1 revenue up 38% and SSSG above 20% in Q2; backing is partial, citing four ATM showroom openings in Q3–Q4 FY27, share gains and volume-led demand, but no order or capacity numbers were given for the growth rate.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects H2 PBT margin to be better than H1 and stable, with gold-on-cash at 42% of exchange and gold-on-cash at 7-8% of exchange supporting stability; Q2 adjusted India EBITDA was ₹496 crore vs ₹432 crore a year earlier.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two ATM showrooms are planned for Q3 and two for Q4 FY27 (four in total), and the company has already drawn up launch plans; the ATM brand is limited to Tamil Nadu for now.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 same-store sales growth was above 20% against single-digit gold price inflation, so growth is volume-led, and early Q3 momentum is good; the planning assumption for Q4 SSS is still about 10%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Surplus cash is to go into existing showrooms, inventory and flagship stores, with a cash-flow deployment plan for FY28 to be shared shortly, but no capex amount was given and the company has not announced a new major plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 38% YoY and management said H1 was ahead of expectations and Q3 is tracking better than estimates, but it kept the ~25% full-year target as a target, not numeric guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 faces a high base and H2 store openings are concentrated in Q4, and wedding buyers defer 15-20 days during gold price volatility, though management is confident and no cut was signalled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said it is moving toward studded and design-led jewellery, and the Tamil Nadu one-gram gold coin B2B contract has begun at small scale with thin margins, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Non-GML debt fully repaid; land monetisation
rows.why: Non-GML debt is fully repaid and 50% of collateral land is released, with one parcel sold for ~₹86-87 crore and another ₹16 crore expected in Q3.

rows.label: ATM regional brand scale-up in Tamil Nadu
rows.why: ATM launched at Chinnanagar in August and management says performance has exceeded expectations, but no metrics were disclosed, and four showrooms are planned in Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Middle East profit decline
rows.why: Middle East revenue rose to ₹960 crore from ₹860 crore and EBITDA to ₹71 crore from ₹61 crore, yet PAT fell to ₹12 crore from ₹15 crore, a risk to watch.

tone.note: Management was confident on festive momentum, H1 ahead of expectations and the ~25% full-year target, but declined to give Q3/Q4 numbers or ATM metrics citing competitive sensitivity; analysts pressed on the sustainability of PBT margins given one-offs, the high Q4 base and the ATM performance.
